title: 3D Floor Plan from Drawing
purpose: Turn an existing architectural drawing into an editable 3D wall shell with separate storeys, spline-derived slabs, and door openings in 3ds Max through Max Ultra MCP.

steps: After importing the ZIP, start a new AI chat and ask the assistant to use 3D Floor Plan from Drawing by Mykhailo Svidryk. Importing alone does not change a scene.

For modeling, connect Max Ultra MCP to the intended 3ds Max scene containing the drawing. Identify the drawing and provide a known dimension with units, wall heights, wall thicknesses where unclear, slab thicknesses, and storey or split-level elevations.

Specify the wall and slab objects to create or edit. Provide door heights and window sill, opening, and top-to-ceiling dimensions where applicable; identify floor-to-ceiling glazing. Resolve numbered questions about ambiguous drawing details before the affected geometry is built.

Request inspection of the completed shell against the drawing in Top, perspective, and relevant section or side views. Check scale, level changes, openings, junctions, editable stacks, and bottom-center pivots. An image alone can support plan review; creating geometry requires a connected scene and authorized changes.
examples: Use 3D Floor Plan from Drawing on the connected scene. Build a wall shell from the existing ground-floor drawing. The marked dimension is 6000 mm, the confirmed wall height is 3000 mm, and slab thickness is 200 mm. Preserve the drawing and ask about unclear lines before modeling.

Build the two storeys shown in this drawing as separate editable wall and slab objects. Align them using the stairwell corners and the supplied elevation schedule. Keep spline sources beneath Extrude.
Inspect this plan for steps and split levels before modeling. Mark ambiguous zones on an actual viewport screenshot and ask for the missing floor and ceiling elevations.

On the designated wall shell, form door lintels with Edit Poly above Extrude. Door heads are 2100 mm above each local finished floor. Keep the confirmed floor-to-ceiling glazing gaps open and preserve the source drawing.
usage.expectedOutput: An editable preliminary 3D shell derived from the supplied drawing, with separate wall and slab objects, confirmed level relationships, requested door openings, and bottom-center pivots. Includes a summary of checks and unresolved details. This is geometry reconstruction from an existing layout, not architectural layout design, finished door/window assemblies, materials, or construction documentation. Examples describe intended use, not tested output quality.

dependencies: For geometry creation: Autodesk 3ds Max with Max Ultra MCP connected to the intended scene and tools for spline, modifier, and scene inspection operations.

An existing architectural drawing, a known dimension with units, and confirmed wall, slab, opening, and level dimensions. An AI client with image input is needed for screenshot-based ambiguity review.
Uses native spline, Extrude, and Edit Poly workflows; no third-party renderer or modeling plugin is specified.

This package includes skill.json and requires an updated Max Ultra MCP build supporting display metadata. As of 2026-10-12, the compatible product implementation is tested but not yet released; earlier numbered skill releases remain available for older importers.
